messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: writing sanity checks in cpp
parts: I am trying to find out the best way to get TMB to exit gracefully if the user gives a silly parameter or data value or contradicting flags. Is it possible to add stop() or error() with an informative message in cpp file?

messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: Re: writing sanity checks in cpp
parts: This is simple, admin can delete this but if anyone else wants to do this we can see it in action from looking at the sam.cpp example https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/3b1beed5b0bfc494cbfc776bbc8bd10fb739c185/tmb_examples/sam.cpp#L162

On Tuesday, August 14, 2018 at 4:23:17 PM UTC+12, Craig Marsh wrote:

I am trying to find out the best way to get TMB to exit gracefully if the user gives a silly parameter or data value or contradicting flags. Is it possible to add stop() or error() with an informative message in cpp file?

messages.author: 3115158bfd890d88
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: writing sanity checks in cpp
parts:
Hi Craig,
I've used the following to debug or break out of user errors when using the MakeADFun

if(model == 8){
    std::cerr<< "Model not yet implemented"<<std::endl; // Output warning
    return 0; // Stop model
  }

Hope that helps!
-Grant

parts:
Thanks for adding that I actually think I prefer your method as it allows you to add more information for example, if you check for Na's in a matrix or an element doesn't satisfy some criteria you could add into your method something like this,

if(my_matrix(i,j) < 0){
    std::cerr <<  "Found value in matrix 'my_matrix' at row " <<  i + 1 << " and col = " << j + 1 << " that was less than zero please check matrix" << std::endl;

return 0; // Stop model
  }

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: writing sanity checks in cpp
parts:
A related problem with std::cerr is that CRAN rejects packages with any std statements (possibly due to the warnings). Because we wanted to get on CRAN, glmmTMB uses error() in the cpp file. 

cheers,
Mollie
